Abadi.text: M.Abadi, L.Cardelli, P-L.Curien, J-J.Levy. Explicit Substitutions (1991).

Granstrom.text: J.G.Granstr\"{o}m. Doctoral thesis: Reference and Computation in Intuitionistic Type Theory (2009). http://intuitionistic.wordpress.com/about/

Kesner.text: D.Kesner. The Theory of Explicit Substitutions Revisited (2007).

nodes.name: Typing rules for the typed calculus with repeated context variables
nodes.statement: (Typing rules). \\ $ \begin{array}{lll} (i)& \Gamma,x:A\vdash x:A &\\[5pt] (ii)& \ruleone{\Gamma\vdash x:A}{\Gamma,y:B\vdash x:A} & (x\not\equiv y) \\[15pt] (iii)& \ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash M:A\arrow B}{\Gamma\vdash N:A}{\Gamma\vdash MN:B} &\\[15pt] (iv)& \ruleone{\Gamma,x:A\vdash M:B}{\Gamma\vdash\lambda x^A.M:A\arrow B} &\\[15pt] (v)& \ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta}{\Delta\vdash M:A}{\Gamma\vdash s\ci M:A} &\\[15pt] (vi)& \Gamma\vdash id\tri\Gamma &\\[5pt] (vii)& \Gamma,x:A\vdash\pi \tri\Gamma &\\[5pt] (viii)& \ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta}{\Gamma\vdash N:A}{\Gamma\vdash \langle s\mi N\is x\rangle\tri\Delta\, ,x:A} &\\[15pt] (ix)& \ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta}{\Delta\vdash q\tri\Sigma}{\Gamma\vdash s\ci q\tri\Sigma} & \end{array} $\\[5pt]
nodes.statement_short: Nine inference rules deriving $\Gamma\vdash M:A$ and $\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta$ over contexts in which variables may repeat.

nodes.name: Derivation of $x:A\mi x:B\mi y:C\vdash x:B$ by rule $(ii)$
nodes.statement: $$ \ruleone{x:A\mi x:B\vdash x:B}{x:A\mi x:B\mi y:C\vdash x:B} $$

nodes.name: Derivation of $x:A\mi x:B\vdash \pi\ci x:A$
nodes.statement: $$ \ruletwo{x:A\mi x:B\vdash \pi\tri x:A}{x:A\vdash x:A}{x:A\mi x:B\vdash \pi\ci x:A} $$

nodes.name: Derivation of $x:A, x:B, y:C\vdash (\pi\ci\pi)\ci x:A$
nodes.statement: $$ \ruletwo{\ruletwo{x:A, x:B, y:C\vdash \pi\tri x:A,x:B}{x:A, x:B\vdash \pi\tri x:A}{x:A, x:B, y:C\vdash\pi\ci\pi\tri x:A}}{x:A\vdash x:A}{x:A, x:B, y:C\vdash (\pi\ci\pi)\ci x:A} $$
nodes.statement_short: Iterated first projection $\pi\ci\pi$ reaches the leftmost occurrence of $x$ in a threefold context.

nodes.name: Derivation of $\vdash\lambda x^A.\lambda x^B.x:A\arrow(B\arrow B)$
nodes.statement: $$ \ruleone{\ruleone{x:A\mi x:B\vdash x:B}{x:A\vdash\lambda x^B.x:B\arrow B}}{\vdash\lambda x^A.\lambda x^B.x:A\arrow(B\arrow B)} $$

nodes.name: Explicit weakening $\Gamma,y:B\vdash \pi\ci M:A$
nodes.statement: $$\ruletwo{\Gamma,y:B\vdash\pi\tri\Gamma}{\ruledot{ \rule{5mm}{0mm} \Gamma\vdash M:A}}{\Gamma,y:B\vdash \pi\ci M:A}$$

nodes.name: Notation $\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}$ for the categorical value of a judgement
nodes.statement: $(\Gamma\vdash M:A)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}\Gamma\overset{f}{\arrow} A$ is shorthand for ``the arrow $\Gamma\overset{f}{\arrow} A$ corresponds to the judgement $\Gamma\vdash M:A$."\\ $(\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Gamma\overset{f}{\arrow} \Delta$ is shorthand for ``the arrow $\Gamma\overset{f}{\arrow} \Delta$ corresponds to the judgement $\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta$."

nodes.name: Values of derivable judgements in cartesian closed categories
nodes.statement: (Values of derivable judgements in cartesian closed categories). \\[5pt] $ \begin{array}{ll} (i)& (\Gamma,x:A\vdash x:A)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Gamma\times A\overset{pr_2}{\arrow}A \\[5pt] (ii)& \ruleone{(\Gamma\vdash x:A)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Gamma\overset{f}{\arrow}A}{(\Gamma,y:B\vdash x:A)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Gamma\times B\overset{pr_1\,\circ\, f}{\arrow}A\using {\quad(x\not\equiv y)}}\\[20pt] (iii)& \ruletwo{(\Gamma\vdash M:A\arrow B)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Gamma\overset{f}{\arrow}B^A}{(\Gamma\vdash N:A)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow } \Gamma\overset{g}{\arrow}A}{(\Gamma\vdash MN:B)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Gamma\overset{\la f\mi g\ra\,\circ\, Ev}{\longrightarrow}B}\\[20pt] (iv)& \ruleone{(\Gamma,x:A\vdash M:B)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow } \Gamma\times A\overset{f}{\arrow}B}{(\Gamma\vdash\lambda x^A.M:A\arrow B)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Gamma\overset{\Lambda (f)}{\arrow}B^A}\\[20pt] (v)& \ruletwo{(\Gamma\vdash s \tri\Delta)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Gamma\overset{f}{\arrow}\Delta }{(\Delta\vdash M:A)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow } \Delta\overset{g}{\arrow}A}{(\Gamma\vdash s \ci M:A)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow } \Gamma\overset{f\,\circ\, g}{\arrow}A}\\[20pt] (vi)& (\Gamma\vdash id \tri\Gamma)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Gamma\overset{id}{\arrow}\Gamma \\[5pt] (vii)& (\Gamma,x:A\vdash\pi \tri\Gamma)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Gamma\times A\overset{pr_1}{\arrow}\Gamma \\[5pt] (viii)& \ruletwo{(\Gamma\vdash s \tri\Delta)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Gamma\overset{f}{\arrow}\Delta }{(\Gamma\vdash N:A)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Gamma\overset{g}{\arrow}A}{(\Gamma\vdash \langle s\mi N\is x\rangle \tri\Delta\, ,x:A)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Gamma\overset{\la f\mi g\rangle }{\arrow}\Delta\times A}\\[20pt] (ix)& \ruletwo{(\Gamma\vdash s \tri\Delta)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Gamma\overset{f}{\arrow}\Delta }{(\Delta\vdash q \tri\Sigma)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Delta\overset{g}{\arrow}\Sigma }{(\Gamma \vdash s \ci q \tri\Sigma)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \Gamma\overset{f\,\circ\, g}{\arrow}\Sigma }\\ \end{array} $
nodes.statement_short: Interprets each derivable judgement as an arrow in a cartesian closed category, by induction over its (unique) derivation.
nodes.definiendum: Values of derivable judgements in cartesian closed categories

nodes.name: The calculus of equations
nodes.statement: (The calculus of equations). \\[5pt] $ \begin{array}{lll} (Beta) & (\lambda x.M)N= \langle id\mi N\is x\rangle\ci M &\\ (Abs) & s\ci \lambda x.M=\lambda x.\langle \pi\ci s\mi x\is x\rangle\ci M &\\ (App) & s\ci (MN)=(s\ci M)(s\ci N) &\\ (ConsVar) & \langle s\mi N\is x\rangle\ci x= N &\\ (New) & \langle s\mi N\is x\rangle\ci y= s\ci y & (x\not\equiv y)\\ (IdVar) & id\ci x= x &\\ (Clos) & s\ci q\ci M= (s\ci q)\ci M &\\ (Ass) & s\ci q\ci r= (s\ci q)\ci r &\\ (IdR) & s\ci id= s &\\ (IdShift) & id\ci \pi=\pi &\\ (ConsShift) & \langle s\mi N\is x\rangle\ci \pi= s &\\ (Map) & s\ci \langle q\mi N\is x\rangle=\langle s\ci q \mi s\ci N\is x\rangle &\\ (\alpha) & \lambda x.M=\lambda y.\langle\pi\mi y\is x\rangle\ci M & (x,y \text{ are arbitrary})\\ [5pt] \end{array}$
nodes.statement_short: An equational presentation with $Beta$, $Abs$, $App$, $ConsVar$, $New$, $IdVar$, $Clos$, $Ass$, $IdR$, $IdShift$, $ConsShift$, $Map$ and $(\alpha)$.

nodes.name: Computation of $(\lambda x y.x)\,y$ in the calculus of equations
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} (\lambda x y.x)\,y & \\ = \langle id\mi y\is x\rangle\ci \lambda y.x & Beta\\ =\lambda y.\langle\pi\ci \langle id\mi y\is x\rangle\mi y\is y\rangle\ci x & Abs\\ =\lambda y.(\pi\ci \langle id\mi y\is x\rangle)\ci x & New\\ =\lambda y.\langle\pi\ci id\mi \pi\ci y\is x\rangle\ci x & Map\\ = \lambda y.\pi\ci y & ConsVar\\ =\lambda z.\langle\pi\mi z\is y\rangle\ci \pi\ci y & \alpha\\ =\lambda z.(\langle\pi\mi z\is y\rangle\ci \pi)\ci y & Clos\\ =\lambda z.\pi\ci y & ConsShift\\ =\lambda z.y & \pi \end{array} $$
nodes.statement_short: A nine-step equational computation renaming the captured bound $y$ to $z$ and ending at $\lambda z.y$.

nodes.name: Derivation of $x:A,x:B\vdash \pi_x\ci x:A$ with subscripted $\pi_x$
nodes.statement: $$ \ruletwo{x:A,x:B\vdash \pi_x\tri x:A}{x:A\vdash x:A}{x:A,x:B\vdash \pi_x\ci x:A} $$

nodes.name: Derivation of $x:A,x:B,y:C\vdash (\pi_y\ci\pi_x)\ci x:A$
nodes.statement: $$ \ruletwo{\ruletwo{x:A,x:B,y:C\vdash \pi_y\tri x:A,x:B}{x:A,x:B\vdash \pi_x\tri x:A}{x:A,x:B,y:C\vdash\pi_y\ci\pi_x\tri x:A}}{x:A\vdash x:A}{x:A,x:B,y:C\vdash (\pi_y\ci\pi_x)\ci x:A} $$
nodes.statement_short: With subscripts, the composite projection records which binder each step passes.

nodes.name: The calculus $\lambda\pi$ without several rules
nodes.statement:
(The calculus $\lambda\pi$ without several rules).\ $  egin{array}{lll} (Beta) & (\lambda x.M)Nightarrow \langle id\mi N\is xangle\ci M &\ (Abs) & s\ci \lambda x.Mightarrow\lambda x.\langle \pi_{x}\ci s\mi x\is xangle\ci M &\ (App) & s\ci (MN)ightarrow(s\ci M)(s\ci N) &\ (ConsVar) & \langle s\mi N\is xangle\ci xightarrow N &\ (New) & \langle s\mi N\is xangle\ci yightarrow s\ci y & (x
ot\equiv y)\ (IdVar) & id\ci xightarrow x &\ (Clos) & s\ci q\ci Mightarrow (s\ci q)\ci M &\ (Ass) & s\ci q\ci rightarrow (s\ci q)\ci r &\ (IdR) & s\ci idightarrow s &\ (IdShift) & id\ci \pi_{x}ightarrow\pi_{x} &\ (ConsShift) & \langle s\mi N\is xangle\ci \pi_{x}ightarrow s &\ (Map) & s\ci \langle q\mi N\is xangleightarrow\langle s\ci q \mi s\ci N\is xangle &\ (\pi_1) & \pi_{x}\ci yightarrow y & (x
ot\equiv y)\ (\pi_2) & (s\ci\pi_{x})\ci yightarrow s\ci y & (x 
ot\equiv y)\ (\alpha_1) & \lambda x.Mightarrow\lambda y.\langle\pi_{y}\mi y\is xangle\ci M & (*) \end{array}$ \ where $(*)$ is some restriction on the variables: if the variable $x$ occurs freely in $\lambda x.M$, we can rename $x$ to a ``good" variable.
nodes.statement_short: A first rewriting version of $\lambda\pi$ with subscripted $\pi_x$, rules $\pi_1,\pi_2$ and the renaming rule $\alpha_1$.

nodes.name: Computation of $(\lambda x y.x)\,y$ with subscripted $\pi$
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} (\lambda x y.x)\,y & \\ \rightarrow\langle id\mi y\is x\rangle\ci \lambda y.x & Beta\\ \rightarrow\lambda y.\langle\pi_y\ci \langle id\mi y\is x\rangle\mi y\is y\rangle\ci x & Abs\\ \rightarrow\lambda y.(\pi_y\ci \langle id\mi y\is x\rangle)\ci x & New\\ \rightarrow\lambda y.\langle\pi_y\ci id\mi \pi_y\ci y\is x\rangle\ci x & Map\\ \rightarrow \lambda y.\pi_y\ci y & ConsVar\\ \rightarrow\lambda z.\langle\pi_z\mi z\is y\rangle\ci \pi_y\ci y & \alpha_1\\ \rightarrow\lambda z.(\langle\pi_z\mi z\is y\rangle\ci \pi_y)\ci y & Clos\\ \rightarrow\lambda z.\pi_z\ci y & ConsShift\\ \rightarrow\lambda z.y & \pi_1 \end{array} $$
nodes.statement_short: The same computation as before, now as a reduction sequence in the subscripted language.

nodes.name: Well-formed terms and substitutions
nodes.statement: (Well-formed terms and substitutions). \\ $ \begin{array}{lll} (i)& \Gamma,x\vdash x &\\[5pt] (ii)& \ruleone{\Gamma\vdash x}{\Gamma,y\vdash x} & (x\not\equiv y) \\[15pt] (iii)& \ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash M}{\Gamma\vdash N}{\Gamma\vdash MN} &\\[15pt] (iv)& \ruleone{\Gamma,x\vdash M}{\Gamma\vdash\lambda x.M} &\\[15pt] (v)& \ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta}{\Delta\vdash M}{\Gamma\vdash s\ci M} &\\[15pt] (vi)& \Gamma\vdash id\tri\Gamma &\\[5pt] (vii)& \Gamma,x\vdash\pi_{x} \tri\Gamma &\\[5pt] (viii)& \ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta}{\Gamma\vdash N}{\Gamma\vdash \langle s\mi N\is x\rangle\tri\Delta ,x} &\\[15pt] (ix)& \ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta}{\Delta\vdash q\tri\Sigma}{\Gamma\vdash s\ci q\tri\Sigma} & \end{array} $
nodes.statement_short: Untyped analogue of the typing rules: nine rules deriving $\Gamma\vdash M$ and $\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta$ over contexts of variables.

nodes.name: Derivation of $x,x,y\vdash x$
nodes.statement: $$ \ruleone{x,x\vdash x}{x,x,y\vdash x} $$

nodes.name: Derivation of $x,x\vdash \pi_x\ci x$
nodes.statement: $$ \ruletwo{x,x\vdash \pi_x\tri x}{x\vdash x}{x,x\vdash \pi_x\ci x} $$

nodes.name: Derivation of $x,x,y\vdash (\pi_y\ci\pi_x)\ci x$
nodes.statement: $$ \ruletwo{\ruletwo{x,x,y\vdash \pi_y\tri x,x}{x,x\vdash \pi_x\tri x}{x,x,y\vdash\pi_y\ci\pi_x\tri x}}{x\vdash x}{x,x,y\vdash (\pi_y\ci\pi_x)\ci x} $$

nodes.name: Derivation of $\vdash\lambda x.\lambda x.x$
nodes.statement: $$ \ruleone{\ruleone{x,x\vdash x}{x\vdash\lambda x.x}}{\vdash\lambda x.\lambda x.x} $$

nodes.name: Compatible closure
nodes.statement: (Compatible closure).\\[10pt] $ \begin{array}{ccc} & \ruleone{ M_1\arrow M_2}{ \lambda x.M_1\arrow\lambda x.M_2}\\[20pt] & \ruleone{ M_1\arrow M_2}{ M_1N\arrow M_2N} & \ruleone{ N_1\arrow N_2}{ MN_1\arrow MN_2}\\[20pt] & \ruleone{ s_1\arrow s_2}{s_1\ci M\arrow s_2\ci M} & \ruleone{ M_1\arrow M_2}{s\ci M_1\arrow s\ci M_2}\\[20pt] & \ruleone{ s_1\arrow s_2}{ \langle s_1\mi N\is x\rangle\arrow \langle s_2\mi N\is x\rangle} & \ruleone{ N_1\arrow N_2}{ \langle s\mi N_1\is x\rangle\arrow \langle s\mi N_2\is x\rangle}\\[20pt] & \ruleone{ s_1\arrow s_2}{ s_1\ci q\arrow s_2\ci q} & \ruleone{ q_1\arrow q_2}{ s\ci q_1\arrow s\ci q_2}\\[20pt] & \ruleone{M_1\arrow M_2}{\Gamma\vdash M_1\ri \Gamma\vdash M_2}\\[20pt] \end{array} $
nodes.statement_short: Congruence rules propagating $\arrow$ through abstraction, application, closure, cons and composition, and lifting it to judgements via $\ri$.

nodes.name: Terms and substitutions of $\lambda\pi$
nodes.statement: The symbols $x,y,z,\ldots$ are \emph{variables}. The symbols $M,N,L$ range over \emph{terms}, $s,q,r$ range over \emph{substitutions}, and $\x,\y,\z$ range over variables (they are \emph{metavariables}). The sets of terms and substitutions are defined inductively as follows: \begin{align*} M,N::&= \x \mid MN \mid \lambda \x. M \mid s\ci M\\ s,q::&= id \mid \pi_{\x} \mid \langle s\mi N\is \x \rangle \mid s\ci q \end{align*} Note that\\[5pt] $\begin{array}{llll} s\ci M & \text{corresponds to} & M[s] &\text{ from ~\cite{Abadi}};\\ s\ci q & \text{corresponds to} & q\ci s &\text{ from ~\cite{Abadi}};\\ \la s\mi N\is \x\ra & \text{corresponds to} & N\cdot s &\text{ from ~\cite{Abadi}};\\ \pi_{\x} & \text{corresponds to} & \uparrow &\text{ from ~\cite{Abadi}}. \end{array}$\\
nodes.statement_short: Inductive grammar for terms ($\x$, $MN$, $\lambda \x.M$, $s\ci M$) and substitutions ($id$, $\pi_{\x}$, $\la s\mi N\is \x\ra$, $s\ci q$), with a dictionary to the notation of~\cite{Abadi}.

nodes.name: Convention on omitted outermost parentheses
nodes.statement: Outermost parentheses are not written.\\ Outermost parentheses around $s$ in $\la s\mi N\is \x\ra$ are not written.\\ Outermost parentheses around $N$ in $\la s\mi N\is \x\ra$ are not written.

nodes.name: Convention on abbreviated application, abstraction and composition
nodes.statement: $ $\\[3pt] $\begin{array}{lll} MN_1\ldots N_k & \text{is shorthand for} & ((MN_1)\ldots)N_k\\ \lambda \x_1\ldots\x_k.M & \text{is shorthand for} & \lambda \x_1.(\ldots(\lambda \x_k.M))\\ \lambda \x.MN_1\ldots N_k & \text{is shorthand for} & \lambda \x.(MN_1\ldots N_k)\\ s\ci MN_1\ldots N_k & \text{is shorthand for} & s\ci(MN_1\ldots N_k)\\ \lambda \x.s\ci M & \text{is shorthand for} & \lambda \x.(s\ci M)\\ s\ci \lambda \x.M & \text{is shorthand for} & s\ci(\lambda \x.M)\\ s_1\ci\ldots\ci s_k\ci s_{k+1} & \text{is shorthand for} & s_1\ci(\ldots\ci(s_k\ci s_{k+1}))\\ s_1\ci \ldots\ci s_k\ci M & \text{is shorthand for} & s_1\ci(\ldots\ci(s_k\ci M))\\ \langle s\mi N_1\is \y_1\mi \ldots\mi N_n\is \y_n \rangle & \text{is shorthand for} & \langle\langle\ldots\la\langle s\mi N_1\is \y_1\rangle\mi N_2\is \y_2\rangle\mi\ldots\rangle\mi N_n\is \y_n\rangle \end{array}$
nodes.statement_short: Fixes left-associated application, iterated abstraction, right-associated composition and iterated cons as shorthands.

nodes.name: Shorthand $id\ci id\ci x$
nodes.statement: $\begin{array}{lll} id\ci id\ci x & \text{is shorthand for} & id\ci (id\ci x) \end{array}$

nodes.name: Shorthand $\lambda x.id\ci y$
nodes.statement: $\begin{array}{lll} \lambda x.id\ci y & \text{is shorthand for} & \lambda x.(id\ci y) \end{array}$

nodes.name: Shorthand $id\ci x(yz)$
nodes.statement: $\begin{array}{lll} id\ci x(yz) & \text{is shorthand for} & id\ci (x(yz)) \end{array}$

nodes.name: Shorthand $\la id\ci id\mi id\ci y\is x\ra$
nodes.statement: $ $\\ $\begin{array}{lll} \la id\ci id\mi id\ci y\is x\ra & \text{is shorthand for} & \la (id\ci id)\mi(id\ci y)\is x\ra\ \end{array}$

nodes.name: Shorthand $id\ci\lambda x.\pi_x\ci\lambda y.z$
nodes.statement: $ $\\ $\begin{array}{lll} id\ci\lambda x.\pi_x\ci\lambda y.z & \text{is shorthand for} & id\ci(\lambda x.(\pi_x\ci(\lambda y.z))) \end{array}$

nodes.name: Shorthand $\la id\mi y\is x\mi z\is x\ra$
nodes.statement: $ $\\ $\begin{array}{lll} \la id\mi y\is x\mi z\is x\ra & \text{is shorthand for} & \la\la id\mi y\is x\ra\mi z\is x\ra \end{array}$

nodes.name: Context
nodes.statement: A \emph{context} is a possibly empty, finite list of variables with multiplicity (i.e., repetitions are permitted). The symbols $\Gamma,\Delta,\Sigma,\Psi$ range over contexts.

nodes.name: The list $x,x,y$ is a context
nodes.statement: The list $x,x,y$ is a context.

nodes.name: Judgement
nodes.statement: A \emph{judgement} is an expression of the form $\Gamma\vdash M$ or of the form $\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta$.
differentia: of the form $\Gamma\vdash M$ or of the form $\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta$

nodes.name: The inference rules for judgements
nodes.statement: (The inference rules for judgements).\\ $ \begin{array}{lll} (i)& \Gamma,\x\vdash \x &\\[5pt] (ii)& \ruleone{\Gamma\vdash \x}{\Gamma,\y\vdash \x} & (\x\neq \y) \\[15pt] (iii)& \ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash M}{\Gamma\vdash N}{\Gamma\vdash MN} &\\[15pt] (iv)& \ruleone{\Gamma,\x\vdash M}{\Gamma\vdash\lambda \x.M} &\\[15pt] (v)& \ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta}{\Delta\vdash M}{\Gamma\vdash s\ci M} &\\[15pt] (vi)& \Gamma\vdash id\tri\Gamma &\\[5pt] (vii)& \Gamma,\x\vdash\pi_{\x} \tri\Gamma &\\[5pt] (viii)& \ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta}{\Gamma\vdash N}{\Gamma\vdash \langle s\mi N\is \x\rangle\tri\Delta ,\x} &\\[15pt] (ix)& \ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta}{\Delta\vdash q\tri\Sigma}{\Gamma\vdash s\ci q\tri\Sigma} & \end{array} $\\
nodes.statement_short: The nine rules $(i)$--$(ix)$ generating the derivable judgements $\Gamma\vdash M$ and $\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta$ of the untyped calculus.

nodes.name: Derivation of $x,x,y\vdash \pi_y\ci\pi_x\ci x$
nodes.statement: $$ \ruletwo{x,x,y\vdash \pi_y\tri x,x}{\ruletwo{x,x\vdash \pi_x\tri x}{x\vdash x}{x,x\vdash \pi_x\ci x}}{x,x,y\vdash \pi_y\ci\pi_x\ci x} $$

nodes.name: Derivation of $\Gamma\vdash (\lambda x.M)N$
nodes.statement: $$ \ruletwo{\ruleone{\ruledot{\Gamma,x\vdash M}}{\Gamma\vdash\lambda x.M}}{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash N}}{\Gamma\vdash (\lambda x.M)N} $$

nodes.name: Derivation of $\Gamma\vdash\la id\mi N\is x\ra\ci M$
nodes.statement: $$ \ruletwo{\ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash id\tri\Gamma}{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash N}}{\Gamma\vdash\la id\mi N\is x\ra\tri\Gamma,x}}{\ruledot{\Gamma,x\vdash M}}{\Gamma\vdash\la id\mi N\is x\ra\ci M} $$

nodes.name: Generation lemma
nodes.statement: $ $\\ Each derivation of $\,\Gamma,\x\vdash \x$ is an application of the rule~(i).\\ Each derivation of $\,\Gamma,\y\vdash \x$ $($where $\x\neq \y)$ is an application of the rule~(ii) to some derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash \x$.\\ Each derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash MN$ is an application of the rule~(iii) to some derivations of $\,\Gamma\vdash M$ and $\,\Gamma\vdash N$.\\ Each derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash \lambda \x.M$ is an application of the rule~(iv) to some derivation of $\,\Gamma,\x\vdash M$.\\ Each derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash s\ci M$ is an application of the rule~(v) to some derivations of $\,\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta$ and $\,\Delta\vdash M$ for some $\Delta$.\\ Each derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash id\tri\Delta$ is an application of the rule~(vi), where $\Delta$ coincides with $\Gamma$.\\ Each derivation of $\,\Delta\vdash \pi_{\x}\tri\Gamma$ is an application of the rule~(vii), where $\Delta$ coincides with $\Gamma,\x$.\\ Each derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash\langle s\mi N\is \x\rangle\tri\Sigma$ is an application of the rule~(viii) to some derivations of $\,\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta$ and $\,\Gamma\vdash N$ for some $\Delta$, where $\Sigma$ coincides with $\Delta,\x$.\\ Each derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash s\ci q\tri\Sigma$ is an application of the rule~(ix) to some derivations of $\,\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta$ and $\,\Delta\vdash q\tri\Sigma$ for some $\Delta$.
nodes.statement_short: Each derivable judgement is obtained by the unique rule matching the shape of its subject.
conclusions: Each derivation of $\,\Gamma,\x\vdash \x$ is an application of the rule~(i).
Each derivation of $\,\Gamma,\y\vdash \x$ $($where $\x\neq \y)$ is an application of the rule~(ii) to some derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash \x$.
Each derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash MN$ is an application of the rule~(iii) to some derivations of $\,\Gamma\vdash M$ and $\,\Gamma\vdash N$.
Each derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash \lambda \x.M$ is an application of the rule~(iv) to some derivation of $\,\Gamma,\x\vdash M$.
Each derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash s\ci M$ is an application of the rule~(v) to some derivations of $\,\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta$ and $\,\Delta\vdash M$ for some $\Delta$.
Each derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash id\tri\Delta$ is an application of the rule~(vi), where $\Delta$ coincides with $\Gamma$.
Each derivation of $\,\Delta\vdash \pi_{\x}\tri\Gamma$ is an application of the rule~(vii), where $\Delta$ coincides with $\Gamma,\x$.

Each derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash\langle s\mi N\is \x\rangle\tri\Sigma$ is an application of the rule~(viii) to some derivations of $\,\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta$ and $\,\Gamma\vdash N$ for some $\Delta$, where $\Sigma$ coincides with $\Delta,\x$.
Each derivation of $\,\Gamma\vdash s\ci q\tri\Sigma$ is an application of the rule~(ix) to some derivations of $\,\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta$ and $\,\Delta\vdash q\tri\Sigma$ for some $\Delta$.

nodes.name: Proof of the Generation lemma
nodes.statement: The proof is straightforward.
nodes.statement_short: Asserted as straightforward: inspect which rule can conclude each syntactic shape.

nodes.name: Uniqueness of the target context $\Delta$ of a substitution
nodes.statement: If a judgement of the form $\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta$ is derivable, then $\Delta$ is uniquely defined for given $\Gamma$ and $s$.
assumptions: a judgement of the form $\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta$ is derivable
conclusions: $\Delta$ is uniquely defined for given $\Gamma$ and $s$.

nodes.name: Proof of uniqueness of $\Delta$
nodes.statement: The proof is by induction over the structure of $s$ (see Definition~\ref{pervoe}).\\ Case 1: $s$ is $id$. This implies that $\Delta$ coincides with $\Gamma$.\\ Case 2: $s$ has the form $\pi_{\x}$ for some $\x$. This implies that $\Gamma$ coincides with $\Delta,\x$.\\ Case 3: $s$ has the form $\langle q\mi N\is \x\rangle$ for some $q,N,\x$. By Generation lemma, we can derive $\Gamma\vdash q\tri\Sigma$ for some $\Sigma$. By the induction hypothesis, $\Sigma$ is uniquely defined for $\Gamma$ and $q$. Then $\Delta$ coincides with $\Sigma,\x$.\\ Case 4: $s$ has the form $q\ci r$ for some $q,r$. By Generation lemma, we can derive $\Gamma\vdash q\tri\Sigma$ for some $\Sigma$. By the induction hypothesis, $\Sigma$ is uniquely defined for $\Gamma$ and $q$. By Generation lemma, we can derive $\Sigma\vdash r\tri\Delta$, where $\Delta$ is uniquely defined for $\Sigma$ and $r$.
nodes.statement_short: Induction over the structure of $s$, with four cases $id$, $\pi_{\x}$, cons and composition.

nodes.name: Uniqueness of derivations
nodes.statement: For any derivable judgement, there is a unique derivation.

nodes.name: Decidability of derivability for judgements
nodes.statement: The problem of derivability for judgements is decidable.
conclusions: The problem of derivability for judgements is decidable.

nodes.name: Proof of decidability of derivability
nodes.statement: We try to construct a derivation from the bottom up.
nodes.statement_short: Construct the derivation bottom-up; the rules are syntax-directed so the search terminates.

nodes.name: $\lambda \x.\pi_{\y}\ci M$ is not well-formed in any context
nodes.statement: Not each term is well-formed in any context. A term of the form $\lambda \x.\pi_{\y}\ci M $ is not well-formed in any context if $\x\neq \y$. $$ \ruleone{\ruletwo{\Gamma,y\vdash \pi_y\tri\Gamma}{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash M}}{\Gamma,x\vdash \pi_y\ci M \using(?)}}{\Gamma\vdash\lambda x.\pi_y\ci M} $$
nodes.statement_short: The subscript of $\pi$ must match the binder, so $\lambda x.\pi_y\ci M$ has no derivation.

nodes.name: $(\pi_{\x}\ci M)(\pi_{\y}\ci N)$ is not well-formed in any context
nodes.statement: A term of the form $(\pi_{\x}\ci M)(\pi_{\y}\ci N)$ is not well-formed in any context if $\x\neq \y$. $$ \ruletwo{\ruletwo{\Gamma,x\vdash\pi_x\tri\Gamma}{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash M}}{\Gamma,x\vdash\pi_x\circ M}} {\ruletwo{\Gamma,y\vdash\pi_y\tri\Gamma}{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash N}}{\Gamma,y\vdash\pi_y\circ N}} {?\vdash(\pi_x\circ M)(\pi_y\circ N)} $$
nodes.statement_short: An application cannot join two closures whose $\pi$ subscripts demand different context extensions.

nodes.name: $\la s\mi N\is \x\ra\ci\pi_{\y}$ is not well-formed in any contexts
nodes.statement: A substitution of the form $\la s\mi N\is \x\ra\ci\pi_{\y}$ is not well-formed in any contexts if $\x\neq \y$. $$ \ruletwo{\ruletwo{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta}}{\Gamma\vdash N}{\Gamma\vdash\la s\mi N\is x\ra\tri\Delta,x}}{\Delta,y\vdash\pi_y\tri\Delta\using(?)}{\Gamma\vdash\la s\mi N\is x\ra\ci\pi_y\tri\Delta} $$
nodes.statement_short: Composing a cons with $\pi_{\y}$ requires $\y$ to be the variable just consed.

nodes.name: Sequences of sets $\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}$ and their union
nodes.statement: The symbols $\mathcal{A,B}$ range over infinite sequences of sets $$\langle \mathcal{A}_1,\mathcal{A}_2,\mathcal{A}_3,\ldots\rangle\in Sets^\omega$$ $$\langle \mathcal{B}_1,\mathcal{B}_2,\mathcal{B}_3,\ldots\rangle\in Sets^\omega$$ By $\mathcal{A}\cup\mathcal{B}$ denote $$\langle\mathcal{A}_1\cup\mathcal{B}_1,\mathcal{A}_2\cup\mathcal{B}_2,\mathcal{A}_3\cup\mathcal{B}_3,\ldots\rangle$$

nodes.name: Free variables of terms
nodes.statement: (Free variables of terms). By definition, put \\ $ \begin{array}{ll} (i) & FV(\x)=\langle \{\x\},\emptyset,\emptyset,\ldots\rangle\\ (ii) & FV(MN)=FV(M)\cup FV(N)\\ (iii) & FV(\lambda \x.M)=O_{\lambda \x}(FV(M))\\ (iv) & FV(s\ci M)=O_s(FV(M)), \end{array} $\\[5pt] where\\[5pt] $ \begin{array}{ll} (v) & O_{\lambda \x}(\mathcal{A})= \langle(\mathcal{A}_1\setminus\{\x\})\cup\mathcal{A}_2\,,\mathcal{A}_3,\mathcal{A}_4,\ldots\rangle\\ (vi) & O_{id}(\mathcal{A})=\mathcal{A}\\ (vii) & O_{\pi_{\x}}(\mathcal{A})=\langle\emptyset,\mathcal{A}_1,\mathcal{A}_2,\ldots\rangle\\ (viii) & O_{s\circ q}(\mathcal{A})=O_s(O_{q}(\mathcal{A}))\\ (ix) & O_{\langle s\mi N\is \x\rangle}(\mathcal{A})=O_s(O_{\lambda \x}(\mathcal{A}))\cup FV(N) \end{array}$
nodes.statement_short: $FV$ maps a term to a sequence of variable sets graded by level, with operators $O_{\lambda \x}$, $O_{id}$, $O_{\pi_{\x}}$, $O_{s\circ q}$ and $O_{\la s\mi N\is \x\ra}$.

nodes.name: Free-variable identities for abstraction, $id$, $\pi_{\x}$ and cons
nodes.statement: $ $\\ $ \begin{array}{l} FV_1(\lambda \x.M)=(FV_1(M)\setminus\{\x\})\cup FV_2(M)\\ FV_{n+1}(\lambda \x.M)=FV_{n+2}(M)\quad (n\geqslant 1)\\ FV(id\ci M)= FV(M)\\ FV_1(\pi_{\x}\ci M)=\emptyset \\ FV_{n+1}(\pi_{\x}\ci M)= FV_{n}(M)\quad (n\geqslant 1)\\ FV(\langle s\mi N\is \x\rangle\ci M)= O_s(O_{\lambda \x}(FV(M)))\cup FV(N) \end{array} $
nodes.statement_short: Level-wise consequences of the definition of $FV$: abstraction shifts levels down, $\pi_{\x}$ shifts them up.
conclusions: FV(\langle s\mi N\is \x\rangle\ci M)= O_s(O_{\lambda \x}(FV(M)))\cup FV(N)

nodes.name: $FV(x)$
nodes.statement: $$FV(x)=\langle\{x\},\emptyset,\emptyset,\ldots\rangle$$

nodes.name: $FV(\pi_y\ci x)$
nodes.statement: $$FV(\pi_y\ci x)=\langle\emptyset,\{x\},\emptyset,\ldots\rangle$$

nodes.name: $FV(\pi_z\ci\pi_y\ci x)$
nodes.statement: $$FV(\pi_z\ci\pi_y\ci x)=\langle\emptyset,\emptyset,\{x\},\emptyset,\ldots\rangle$$

nodes.name: $FV(\lambda z.\pi_z\ci\pi_y\ci x)$
nodes.statement: $$FV(\lambda z.\pi_z\ci\pi_y\ci x)=\langle\emptyset,\{x\},\emptyset,\ldots\rangle$$

nodes.name: $FV(\lambda y z.\pi_z\ci\pi_y\ci x)$
nodes.statement: $$FV(\lambda y z.\pi_z\ci\pi_y\ci x)=\langle\{x\},\emptyset,\emptyset,\ldots\rangle$$

nodes.name: $FV(\lambda x y z.\pi_z\ci\pi_y\ci x)$
nodes.statement: $$FV(\lambda x y z.\pi_z\ci\pi_y\ci x)=\langle\emptyset,\emptyset,\emptyset,\ldots\rangle$$

nodes.name: $FV(x\,(\pi_z\ci\pi_y\ci x))$
nodes.statement: $$FV(x\,(\pi_z\ci\pi_y\ci x))=\langle\{x\},\emptyset,\{x\},\emptyset,\ldots\rangle$$

nodes.name: $FV(\lambda z.x\,(\pi_z\ci \pi_y\ci x))$
nodes.statement: $$FV(\lambda z.x\,(\pi_z\ci \pi_y\ci x))=\langle\{x\},\{x\},\emptyset,\ldots\rangle$$

nodes.name: $FV(\lambda y z.x\,(\pi_z\ci\pi_y\ci x))$
nodes.statement: $$FV(\lambda y z.x\,(\pi_z\ci\pi_y\ci x))=\langle\{x\},\emptyset,\emptyset,\ldots\rangle$$

nodes.name: $FV(\lambda x y z.x\,(\pi_z\ci\pi_y\ci x))$
nodes.statement: $$FV(\lambda x y z.x\,(\pi_z\ci\pi_y\ci x))=\langle\emptyset,\emptyset,\emptyset,\ldots\rangle$$

nodes.name: $FV(\pi_x\ci x)$
nodes.statement: $FV(\pi_x\ci x)=\la\emptyset,\{x\},\emptyset,\emptyset,\ldots\ra$

nodes.name: $FV(\lambda x.\pi_x\ci x)$ -- a binder that does not bind
nodes.statement: $FV(\lambda x.\pi_x\ci x)=\la\{x\},\emptyset,\emptyset,\ldots\ra$

nodes.name: $(s\ci q)\ci M$ and $s\ci q\ci M$ have the same $FV$
nodes.statement: $(s\ci q)\ci M$ and $s\ci q\ci M$ have the same $FV$ .
conclusions: $(s\ci q)\ci M$ and $s\ci q\ci M$ have the same $FV$

nodes.name: Proof that $(s\ci q)\ci M$ and $s\ci q\ci M$ have the same $FV$
nodes.statement: The proof is straightforward.
nodes.statement_short: Asserted as straightforward: both sides unfold to $O_s(O_q(FV(M)))$.

nodes.name: $\la s\mi N\is \x\ra\ci M$ and $(s\ci\lambda \x.M)N$ have the same $FV$
nodes.statement: $\langle s\mi N\is \x\rangle\circ M$ and $(s\circ \lambda \x.M)N$ have the same $FV$.
conclusions: $\langle s\mi N\is \x\rangle\circ M$ and $(s\circ \lambda \x.M)N$ have the same $FV$

nodes.name: Proof that cons and the encoded application have the same $FV$
nodes.statement: The proof is straightforward.
nodes.statement_short: Asserted as straightforward: unfold clause $(ix)$ of the definition of $FV$.

nodes.name: Convention writing $O_{\pi}$ for $O_{\pi_{\x}}$
nodes.statement: Since $O_{\pi_{\x}}$ and $O_{\pi_{\y}}$ are the same for any $\x,\y$, we will simply write $O_{\pi}$.

nodes.name: Inclusion $\mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathcal{B}$ of sequences of sets
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathcal{B}$ is shorthand for ``$\mathcal{A}_i\subseteq\mathcal{B}_i$ for all $i\geqslant 1$."

nodes.name: Monotonicity of $O_{\lambda \x}$ and $O_{\pi}$ with respect to $\subseteq$
nodes.statement: $O_{\lambda \x}$ and $O_{\pi}$ are monotone operators with respect to $\subseteq$ (for any $\x$).
conclusions: $O_{\lambda \x}$ and $O_{\pi}$ are monotone operators with respect to $\subseteq$ (for any $\x$)

nodes.name: Proof of monotonicity of $O_{\lambda \x}$ and $O_{\pi}$
nodes.statement: The proof is straightforward.
nodes.statement_short: Asserted as straightforward: both operators act level-wise by union and shift.

nodes.name: Monotonicity of $O_s$ with respect to $\subseteq$
nodes.statement: $O_s$ is monotone with respect to $\subseteq$ for any $s$.
conclusions: $O_s$ is monotone with respect to $\subseteq$ for any $s$.

nodes.name: Iterated abstraction $\lambda\Gamma.M$ over a context
nodes.statement: We define $\lambda\Gamma.M$ as follows: \\ $ \begin{array}{ll} & \lambda\,nil.M \equiv M\\ & \lambda\Sigma,\x.M \equiv\lambda\Sigma.(\lambda \x.M), \end{array} $\\[5pt] where $nil$ is the empty context. For example, $$\lambda x,y,z.M\equiv\lambda xyz.M$$

nodes.name: Free variables of judgements
nodes.statement: (Free variables of judgements). By definition, put\\ $ \begin{array}{ll} & FV(\Gamma\vdash M)=FV(\lambda\Gamma.M)\\ \end{array} $

nodes.name: $\Uparrow_{\Delta}\!(s)$
nodes.statement: We define $\Uparrow_{\Delta}\!(s)$ as follows: \\ $ \begin{array}{ll} & \Uparrow_{nil}(s) \equiv s\\ & \Uparrow_{\Sigma,\x}(s) \equiv\langle\pi_{\x}\,\ci\Uparrow_{\Sigma}\!(s)\mi \x\is \x\rangle, \end{array} $\\[5pt] where $nil$ is the empty context. For example, $$\Uparrow_{x,y,z}\!(s)\equiv\langle\pi_{z}\ci\langle\pi_{y}\ci\langle\pi_{x}\ci s\mi x\is x\rangle\mi y\is y\rangle\mi z\is z\rangle$$
nodes.statement_short: Lifts a substitution through a whole context by iterating $\la\pi_{\x}\ci -\mi \x\is \x\ra$.

nodes.name: Convention $\Uparrow_{\Delta}\!\la s\mi N\is \x\ra$
nodes.statement: $ $\\ $ \begin{array}{lll} \Uparrow_{\Delta}\!\la s\mi N\is \x\ra & \text{is shorthand for} & \Uparrow_{\Delta}\!(\la s\mi N\is \x\ra) \end{array} $

nodes.name: The calculus $\lambda\pi$
nodes.statement:
(The calculus $\lambda\pi$).\[10pt] $  egin{array}{ccc} & uleone{ M_1\arrow M_2}{ \lambda \x.M_1\arrow\lambda \x.M_2}\[20pt] & uleone{ M_1\arrow M_2}{ M_1N\arrow M_2N} & uleone{ N_1\arrow N_2}{ MN_1\arrow MN_2}\[20pt] & uleone{ s_1\arrow s_2}{s_1\ci M\arrow s_2\ci M} & uleone{ M_1\arrow M_2}{s\ci M_1\arrow s\ci M_2}\[20pt] & uleone{ s_1\arrow s_2}{ \langle s_1\mi N\is \xangle\arrow \langle s_2\mi N\is \xangle} & uleone{ N_1\arrow N_2}{ \langle s\mi N_1\is \xangle\arrow \langle s\mi N_2\is \xangle}\[20pt] & uleone{ s_1\arrow s_2}{ s_1\ci q\arrow s_2\ci q} & uleone{ q_1\arrow q_2}{ s\ci q_1\arrow s\ci q_2}\[20pt] & uleone{M_1\arrow M_2}{\Gamma\vdash M_1i \Gamma\vdash M_2}\[20pt] \end{array} $ $  egin{array}{lll} (Beta) & (\lambda \x.M)Nightarrow \langle id\mi N\is \xangle\ci M &\ (Abs) & s\ci \lambda \x.Mightarrow\lambda \x.\langle \pi_{\x}\ci s\mi \x\is \xangle\ci M &\ (App) & s\ci MNightarrow(s\ci M)(s\ci N) &\ (ConsVar) & \langle s\mi N\is \xangle\ci \xightarrow N &\ (New) & \langle s\mi N\is \xangle\ci \yightarrow s\ci \y & (\x

eq \y)\ (\pi_2) & (s\ci\pi_{\x})\ci \yightarrow s\ci \y & (\x 
eq \y)\ (\alpha_1) & \lambda \x.Mightarrow\lambda \y.\langle\pi_{\y}\mi \y\is \xangle\ci M & (*)\ (\alpha_2) & \Gamma,\x,\Delta\vdash Mi\Gamma,\y,\Delta\vdash\, \Uparrow_{\Delta}\!\langle\pi_{\y}\mi \y\is \xangle\ci M & (**) \[5pt] \end{array}$\ where the side conditions are as follows:\[5pt] $  egin{array}{ll} (*) & \x \in  igcup_{i\geqslant 1} FV_i(\lambda \x.M);\quad \y
otin  igcup_{i\geqslant 1} FV_i(\lambda \x.M )\ (**) & \x\in  igcup_{i\geqslant 1} FV_i(\x,\Delta\vdash M);\quad \y
otin  igcup_{i\geqslant 1}FV_i(\x,\Delta\vdash M )\ \end{array}\[5pt] $ Recall that $s\ci MN$ is shorthand for $s\ci(MN)$.\
nodes.statement_short: The full rewriting system: compatible closure, the substitution rules $Beta$--$Map$, the projection rules $\pi_1,\pi_2$, and the two renaming rules $\alpha_1$ (terms) and $\alpha_2$ (judgements) with their freshness side conditions.

nodes.name: Reflexive transitive closures $\twoh$ and $\ri\ri$
nodes.statement: By $\twoh$ denote the reflexive transitive closure of $\arrow$.\\ By $\ri\ri$ denote the reflexive transitive closure of $\ri$.

nodes.name: A cons chain applied to $\x$ reduces to $N$
nodes.statement: $ $\\ If $\x\neq \y_1, \ldots, \x\neq \y_k$, then $\la s\mi N\is \x\mi N_1\is \y_1\mi\ldots\mi N_k\is \y_k\ra\ci \x\twoh N$.

nodes.name: Proof that a cons chain applied to $\x$ reduces to $N$
nodes.statement: We use $New$ (repeatedly), then we use $ConsVar$.
nodes.statement_short: Peel the later bindings with $New$, then finish with $ConsVar$.

nodes.name: $\la id\mi N\is x\mi L\is y\ra\ci x\twoh N$
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} \langle id\mi N\is x\mi L\is y\rangle\ci x & \\ \rightarrow\langle id\mi N\is x\rangle\ci x & New\\ \rightarrow N & ConsVar \end{array}$$

nodes.name: $\la id\mi N\is x\mi L\is y\ra\ci y\arrow L$
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} \langle id\mi N\is x\mi L\is y\rangle\ci y & \\ \rightarrow L & ConsVar \end{array}$$

nodes.name: $\la id\mi N\is x\mi L\is y\ra\ci z\twoh z$
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} \langle id\mi N\is x\mi L\is y\rangle\ci z & \\ \rightarrow\langle id\mi N\is x\rangle\ci z & New\\ \rightarrow id\ci z & New\\ \rightarrow z & IdVar \end{array}$$

nodes.name: Rightmost binding wins: $\la id\mi N\is x\mi L\is x\ra\ci x\arrow L$
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} \langle id\mi N\is x\mi L\is x\rangle\ci x & \\ \rightarrow L & ConsVar \end{array}$$

nodes.name: $\la id\mi N\is x\mi L\is x\ra\ci \pi_x\ci x\twoh N$
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} \langle id\mi N\is x\mi L\is x\rangle\ci \pi_x\ci x & \\ \arrow(\langle id\mi N\is x\mi L\is x\rangle\ci \pi_x)\ci x & Clos\\ \arrow \langle id\mi N\is x\ra\ci x & ConsShift\\ \rightarrow N & ConsVar \end{array}$$
nodes.statement_short: $\pi_x$ discards the rightmost binding, so the earlier one is reached.

nodes.name: $\la \pi_x\mi N\is y\mi L\is y\ra\ci z\twoh z$
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} \langle \pi_x\mi N\is y\mi L\is y\rangle\ci z & \\ \rightarrow\langle \pi_x\mi N\is y\rangle\ci z & New\\ \rightarrow\pi_x\ci z & New\\ \rightarrow z & \pi_1 \end{array}$$

nodes.name: A normal form $\pi_x\ci x$
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} \langle\pi_x\mi N\is y\mi L\is y\rangle\ci x & \\ \rightarrow\langle\pi_x\mi N\is y\rangle\ci x & New\\ \rightarrow\pi_x\ci x & New \end{array}$$ where $\pi_x\ci x$ is a normal form.
nodes.statement_short: Reduction gets stuck at $\pi_x\ci x$, the normal form motivating the rule $\alpha_2$.

nodes.name: $FV(\lambda x.\pi_x\ci x)$
nodes.statement: $FV(\lambda x.\pi_x\ci x)=\la\{x\},\emptyset,\emptyset,\ldots\ra$

nodes.name: Renaming $\lambda x.\pi_x\ci x$ to $\lambda y.x$ by $\alpha_1$
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} \lambda x.\pi_x\ci x & \\ \rightarrow\lambda y.\langle\pi_y\mi y\is x\rangle\ci \pi_x\ci x & \alpha_1\\ \rightarrow\lambda y.(\langle\pi_y\mi y\is x\rangle\ci \pi_x)\ci x & Clos\\ \rightarrow\lambda y.\pi_y\ci x & ConsShift\\ \rightarrow\lambda y.x & \pi_1 \end{array}$$
nodes.statement_short: $\alpha_1$ frees the shadowed occurrence, after which $ConsShift$ and $\pi_1$ finish the reduction.

nodes.name: Reduction of $(\lambda x y.x)\,y$ in $\lambda\pi$
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} (\lambda x y.x)\,y & \\ \rightarrow\langle id\mi y\is x\rangle\ci \lambda y.x & Beta\\ \rightarrow\lambda y.\langle\pi_y\ci \langle id\mi y\is x\rangle\mi y\is y\rangle\ci x & Abs\\ \rightarrow\lambda y.(\pi_y\ci \langle id\mi y\is x\rangle)\ci x & New\\ \rightarrow\lambda y.\langle\pi_y\ci id\mi \pi_y\ci y\is x\rangle\ci x & Map\\ \rightarrow \lambda y.\pi_y\ci y & ConsVar\\ \rightarrow\lambda z.\langle\pi_z\mi z\is y\rangle\ci \pi_y\ci y & \alpha_1\\ \rightarrow\lambda z.(\langle\pi_z\mi z\is y\rangle\ci \pi_y)\ci y & Clos\\ \rightarrow\lambda z.\pi_z\ci y & ConsShift\\ \rightarrow\lambda z.y & \pi_1 \end{array} $$
nodes.statement_short: Nine steps: $Beta$, $Abs$, $New$, $Map$, $ConsVar$, $\alpha_1$, $Clos$, $ConsShift$, $\pi_1$.

nodes.name: An alternative reduction of $(\lambda x y.x)\,y$
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} (\lambda x y.x)\,y & \\ \rightarrow \langle id\mi y\is x\rangle\ci\lambda y.x & Beta\\ \rightarrow\lambda y.\langle\pi_y\ci\langle id\mi y\is x\rangle\mi y\is y\rangle\ci x & Abs\\ \rightarrow\lambda y.\langle\pi_y\ci id\mi \pi_y\ci y\is x\mi y\is y\rangle\ci x & Map\\ \rightarrow\lambda y.\langle\pi_y\ci id\mi \pi_y\ci y\is x\rangle\ci x & New\\ \rightarrow \lambda y.\pi_y\ci y & ConsVar\\ \rightarrow\lambda z.\langle\pi_z\mi z\is y\rangle\ci \pi_y\ci y & \alpha_1\\ \rightarrow\lambda z.(\langle\pi_z\mi z\is y\rangle\ci \pi_y)\ci y & Clos\\ \rightarrow\lambda z.\pi_z\ci y & ConsShift\\ \rightarrow\lambda z.y & \pi_1 \end{array}$$
nodes.statement_short: The same term reduced with $Map$ before $New$, reaching the same result $\lambda z.y$.

nodes.name: $FV(x\vdash\pi_x\ci x)$
nodes.statement: $FV(x\vdash\pi_x\ci x)=FV(\lambda x.\pi_x\ci x)=\la\{x\},\emptyset,\emptyset,\ldots\ra$

nodes.name: Renaming in a context: $x,x\vdash \pi_x\ci x$ under $\alpha_2$
nodes.statement: $$ x,x\vdash \pi_x\ci x \ri_{\alpha_2} x,y\vdash\langle\pi_y\mi y\is x\rangle\ci \pi_x\ci x$$ Further, $$\begin{array}{ll} \langle \pi_y\mi y\is x\rangle\ci \pi_x\ci x & \\ \rightarrow (\langle \pi_y\mi y\is x\rangle\ci \pi_x)\ci x & Clos\\ \rightarrow \pi_y\ci x & ConsShift\\ \rightarrow x & \pi_1 \end{array}$$ We see that $$\begin{array}{ll} x,x\vdash \pi_x\ci x & \\ \ri x,y\vdash\langle\pi_y\mi y\is x\rangle\ci \pi_x\ci x & \alpha_2\\ \ri x,y\vdash (\langle \pi_y\mi y\is x\rangle\ci \pi_x)\ci x & Clos\\ \ri x,y\vdash \pi_y\ci x & ConsShift\\ \ri x,y\vdash x & \pi_1 \end{array}$$
nodes.statement_short: $\alpha_2$ renames a context variable, unblocking the stuck term $\pi_x\ci x$ so that it reduces to $x$.

nodes.name: $FV(\lambda x z.\pi_z\ci\pi_x\ci x)$
nodes.statement: $FV(\lambda x z.\pi_z\ci\pi_x\ci x)=\la\{x\},\emptyset,\emptyset,\ldots\ra$

nodes.name: Reduction of $\lambda x x z.\pi_z\ci\pi_x\ci x$
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} \lambda x x z.\pi_z\ci\pi_x\ci x & \\ \arrow \lambda x y.\la\pi_y\mi y\is x\ra\ci\lambda z.\pi_z\ci\pi_x\ci x & \alpha_1\\ \arrow \lambda x y z.\Uparrow_z\!\la\pi_y\mi y\is x\ra\ci\pi_z\ci\pi_x\ci x & Abs\\ \equiv\lambda x y z.\la\pi_z\ci\la\pi_y\mi y\is x\ra\mi z\is z\ra\ci\pi_z\ci\pi_x\ci x & Definition~\ref{uparrow}\\ \arrow \lambda x y z.(\la\pi_z\ci\la\pi_y\mi y\is x\ra\mi z\is z\ra\ci\pi_z)\ci\pi_x\ci x & Clos\\ \arrow \lambda x y z.(\pi_z\ci\la\pi_y\mi y\is x\ra)\ci\pi_x\ci x & ConsShift\\ \arrow \lambda x y z.\la\pi_z\ci\pi_y\mi\pi_z\ci y\is x\ra\ci\pi_x\ci x & Map\\ \arrow \lambda x y z.(\la\pi_z\ci\pi_y\mi\pi_z\ci y\is x\ra\ci\pi_x)\ci x & Clos\\ \arrow \lambda x y z.(\pi_z\ci\pi_y)\ci x & ConsShift\\ \arrow \lambda x y z.\pi_z\ci x & \pi_2\\ \arrow \lambda x y z. x & \pi_1 \end{array}$$
nodes.statement_short: A ten-step reduction using $\alpha_1$, $Abs$, $Clos$, $ConsShift$, $Map$, $\pi_2$ and $\pi_1$.

nodes.name: $FV(x,z\vdash\pi_z\ci\pi_x\ci x)$
nodes.statement: $FV(x,z\vdash\pi_z\ci\pi_x\ci x)=FV(\lambda x z.\pi_z\ci\pi_x\ci x)=\la\{x\},\emptyset,\emptyset,\ldots\ra$

nodes.name: Reduction of the judgement $x,x,z\vdash\pi_z\ci\pi_x\ci x$
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} x,x,z\vdash\pi_z\ci\pi_x\ci x & \\ \ri x,y,z\vdash\,\Uparrow_z\!\la\pi_y\mi y\is x\ra\ci\pi_z\ci\pi_x\ci x & \alpha_2\\ \equiv x,y,z\vdash\la\pi_z\ci\la\pi_y\mi y\is x\ra\mi z\is z\ra\ci\pi_z\ci\pi_x\ci x & Definition~\ref{uparrow}\\ \ri x,y,z\vdash(\la\pi_z\ci\la\pi_y\mi y\is x\ra\mi z\is z\ra\ci\pi_z)\ci\pi_x\ci x & Clos\\ \ri x,y,z\vdash(\pi_z\ci\la\pi_y\mi y\is x\ra)\ci\pi_x\ci x & ConsShift\\ \ri x,y,z\vdash\la\pi_z\ci\pi_y\mi\pi_z\ci y\is x\ra\ci\pi_x\ci x & Map\\ \ri x,y,z\vdash(\la\pi_z\ci\pi_y\mi\pi_z\ci y\is x\ra\ci\pi_x)\ci x & Clos\\ \ri x,y,z\vdash(\pi_z\ci\pi_y)\ci x & ConsShift\\ \ri x,y,z\vdash\pi_z\ci x & \pi_2\\ \ri x,y,z\vdash x & \pi_1 \end{array}$$
nodes.statement_short: The judgement-level analogue of the previous reduction, driven by $\alpha_2$.

nodes.name: Reduction of $(\lambda x y z.xz(yz))(\lambda x y.x)$
nodes.statement: (Some redexes are underlined).\\ $$\begin{array}{ll} (\lambda x y z.xz(yz))(\lambda x y.x) & \\ \arrow \la id\mi \lambda x y.x\is x\ra\ci\lambda y z.xz(yz) & Beta\\ \arrow \lambda y.\Uparrow_{y}\!\la id\mi \lambda x y.x\is x\ra\ci\lambda z. xz(yz) & Abs\\ \arrow \lambda y z.\Uparrow_{y,z}\!\!\la id\mi \lambda x y.x\is x\ra\ci xz(yz) & Abs\\ \arrow \lambda y z.(\underline{\Uparrow_{y,z}\!\!\la id\mi \lambda x y.x\is x\ra\ci xz})\,(\Uparrow_{y,z}\!\!\la id\mi \lambda x y.x\is x\ra\ci yz) & App\\ \twoh \lambda y z.(\lambda x y.x)\,z\,(\underline{\Uparrow_{y,z}\!\!\la id\mi \lambda x y.x\is x\ra\ci yz}) & App, Example~\ref{4.25},Example~\ref{4.26}\\ \twoh \lambda y z.(\lambda x y.x)\,z\,(yz) & App,Example~\ref{4.27},Example~\ref{4.26}\\ \arrow \lambda y z.(\la id\mi z\is x\ra\ci\lambda y.x)(yz) & Beta\\ \arrow \lambda y z.(\lambda y.\underline{\Uparrow_y\!\la id\mi z\is x\ra\ci x})(yz) & Abs\\ \twoh \lambda y z.(\lambda y. z)(yz) & Example~\ref{4.28}\\ \arrow \lambda y z.\la id\mi yz\is y\ra\ci z & Beta\\ \arrow \lambda y z.id\ci z & New\\ \arrow \lambda y z.z & IdVar \end{array}$$
nodes.statement_short: A full computation of the combinator application, delegating three sub-reductions to later examples.

nodes.name: Sub-reduction $\Uparrow_{y,z}\!\la id\mi \lambda xy.x\is x\ra\ci x\twoh\lambda x y.x$
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} \Uparrow_{y,z}\!\la id\mi \lambda xy.x\is x\ra\ci x & \\ \equiv\la\pi_z\ci\Uparrow_y\!\la id\mi \lambda xy.x\is x\ra\mi y\is y\ra\ci x & Definition~\ref{uparrow}\\ \arrow(\pi_z\ci\Uparrow_y\! \la id\mi \lambda xy.x\is x\ra)\ci x & New\\ \equiv(\pi_z\ci\la\pi_y\ci \la id\mi \lambda xy.x\is x\ra\mi y\is y\ra)\ci x & Definition~\ref{uparrow}\\ \arrow\la\pi_z\ci\pi_y\ci\la id\mi \lambda xy.x\is x\ra\mi \pi_z\ci y\is y\ra\ci x & Map\\ \arrow(\pi_z\ci\pi_y\ci\la id\mi \lambda xy.x\is x\ra)\ci x & New\\ \arrow(\pi_z\ci\la\pi_y\ci id\mi \pi_y\ci\lambda xy.x\is x\ra)\ci x & Map\\ \arrow\la\pi_z\ci\pi_y\ci id\mi\pi_z\ci\pi_y\ci\lambda xy.x\is x\ra\ci x & Map\\ \arrow\pi_z\ci\pi_y\ci\lambda xy.x & ConsVar\\ \twoh \lambda x y.x & because\,\, \lambda xy.x\,\, is\,\, closed \end{array}$$
nodes.statement_short: Unfolding $\Uparrow_{y,z}$ and applying $Map$/$ConsVar$ retrieves the substituted closed term.

nodes.name: Sub-reduction $\Uparrow_{y,z}\!\la id\mi \lambda xy.x\is x\ra\ci z\arrow z$
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} \Uparrow_{y,z}\!\la id\mi \lambda xy.x\is x\ra\ci z & \\ \equiv\la\pi_z\ci \Uparrow_y\!\la id\mi \lambda xy.x\is x\ra\mi z\is z\ra\ci z & Definition~\ref{uparrow}\\ \arrow z & ConsVar \end{array}$$

nodes.name: Sub-reduction $\Uparrow_{y,z}\!\la id\mi\lambda xy.x\is x\ra\ci y\twoh y$
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} \Uparrow_{y,z}\!\la id\mi\lambda xy.x\is x\ra\ci y & \\ \equiv\la\pi_z\ci\Uparrow_y\!\la id\mi \lambda xy.x\is x\ra\mi z\is z\ra\ci y & Definition~\ref{uparrow}\\ \arrow(\pi_z\ci\Uparrow_y\!\la id\mi \lambda xy.x\is x\ra)\ci y & New\\ \equiv(\pi_z\ci\la\pi_y\ci\la id\mi\lambda xy.x\is x\ra\mi y\is y\ra)\ci y & Definition~\ref{uparrow}\\ \arrow\la\pi_z\ci\pi_y\ci\la id\mi \lambda xy.x\is x\ra\mi \pi_z\ci y\is y\ra\ci y & Map\\ \arrow \pi_z\ci y & ConsVar\\ \arrow y & \pi_1 \end{array}$$
nodes.statement_short: Unfolding the lift and applying $New$, $Map$, $ConsVar$ and $\pi_1$ returns $y$.

nodes.name: Sub-reduction $\Uparrow_y\!\la id\mi z\is x\ra\ci x\twoh z$
nodes.statement: $$\begin{array}{ll} \Uparrow_y\!\la id\mi z\is x\ra\ci x & \\ \equiv\la\pi_y\ci\la id\mi z\is x\ra\mi y\is y\ra\ci x & Definition~\ref{uparrow}\\ \arrow(\pi_y\ci\la id\mi z\is x\ra)\ci x & New\\ \arrow\la\pi_y\ci id\mi\pi_y\ci z\is x\ra\ci x & Map\\ \arrow\pi_y\ci z & ConsVar\\ \arrow z & \pi_1 \end{array}$$
nodes.statement_short: The lifted substitution still delivers $z$ for $x$ under one extra binder.

nodes.name: Subject reduction, part one
nodes.statement: $ $\\ If $\Gamma\vdash M_1$ is derivable and $M_1\arrow M_2$, then $\Gamma\vdash M_2$ is derivable.\\ If $\Gamma\vdash s_1\tri\Delta$ is derivable and $s_1\arrow s_2$, then $\Gamma\vdash s_2\tri\Delta$ is derivable.
nodes.statement_short: $\arrow$-reduction preserves derivability of $\Gamma\vdash M$ and of $\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta$.

nodes.name: Proof of Subject reduction, part one
nodes.statement: The proof is straightforward, but tedious.\\[5pt] Case $Beta. \quad (\lambda \x.M)N\rightarrow \langle id\mi N\is \x\rangle\ci M $\\[5pt] $$\ruletwo{\ruleone{\ruledot{\Gamma,\x\vdash M}}{\Gamma\vdash\lambda \x.M}}{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash N}}{\Gamma\vdash (\lambda \x.M)N}$$\\[5pt] $$\ruletwo{\ruletwo{\Gamma\vdash id\tri\Gamma}{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash N}}{\Gamma\vdash\la id\mi N\is \x\ra\tri\Gamma,\x}}{\ruledot{\Gamma,\x\vdash M}}{\Gamma\vdash\la id\mi N\is \x\ra\ci M}$$\\[5pt] Case $Abs. \quad s\ci \lambda \x.M\rightarrow\lambda \x.\langle \pi_{\x}\ci s\mi \x\is \x\rangle\ci M $\\[5pt] $$\ruletwo{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta}}{\ruleone{\ruledot{\Delta,\x\vdash M}}{\Delta\vdash\lambda \x.M}}{\Gamma\vdash s\ci\lambda \x.M}$$\\[5pt] $$\ruleone{\ruletwo{\ruletwo{\ruletwo{\Gamma,\x\vdash\pi_{\x}\tri\Gamma}{\ruledot{\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta}}{\Gamma,\x\vdash\pi_{\x}\ci s\tri\Delta}}{\Gamma,\x\vdash \x}{\Gamma,\x\vdash\la\pi_{\x}\ci s\mi \x\is \x\ra\tri\Delta,\x}}{\ruledot{\Delta,\x\vdash M}}{\Gamma,\x\vdash\la\pi_{\x}\ci s\mi \x\is \x\ra\ci M}}{\Gamma\vdash\lambda \x.\la\pi_{\x}\ci s\mi \x\is \x\ra\ci M}$$\\[5pt] Case $\alpha_1$. $ \lambda \x.M\rightarrow\lambda \y.\langle\pi_{\y}\mi \y\is \x\rangle\ci M $ $\quad (*)$ \\[5pt] $$\ruleone{\ruledot{\Gamma,\x\vdash M}}{\Gamma\vdash\lambda \x.M}$$\\[5pt] $$\ruleone{\ruletwo{\ruletwo{\Gamma,\y\vdash\pi_{\y}\tri\Gamma}{\Gamma,\y\vdash \y}{\Gamma,\y\vdash\la\pi_{\y}\mi \y\is \x\ra\tri\Gamma,\x}}{\ruledot{\Gamma,\x\vdash M}}{\Gamma,\y\vdash\la\pi_{\y}\mi \y\is \x\ra\ci M}}{\Gamma\vdash\lambda \y.\la\pi_{\y}\mi \y\is \x\ra\ci M}$$\\[5pt] And so on. Note that we do not use $(*)$ in the proof of the case $\alpha_1$.
nodes.statement_short: Case analysis on the contracted redex, exhibiting the derivation of the reduct for $Beta$, $Abs$ and $\alpha_1$.

nodes.name: Derivability of $\lambda \x.\!\Uparrow_{\x}\!(s)\ci M$
nodes.statement: If $\Gamma\vdash s\ci\lambda \x.M$ is derivable, then $\Gamma\vdash\lambda \x.\!\Uparrow_{\x}\!(s) \ci M$ is derivable.

nodes.name: Proof of derivability of $\lambda \x.\!\Uparrow_{\x}\!(s)\ci M$
nodes.statement: Theorem~\ref{SubRed1}, the case $Abs$.
nodes.statement_short: Instance of the $Abs$ case of Subject reduction, part one.

nodes.name: Derivability of $\lambda \Delta.\!\Uparrow_{\Delta}\!(s)\ci M$
nodes.statement: If $\Gamma\vdash s\ci\lambda\Delta.M$ is derivable, then $\Gamma\vdash\lambda \Delta.\!\Uparrow_{\Delta}\!(s)\ci M$ is derivable.

nodes.name: Proof of derivability of $\lambda \Delta.\!\Uparrow_{\Delta}\!(s)\ci M$
nodes.statement: Recall that $\Uparrow_{\Sigma,\x}\!(s)\equiv\,\Uparrow_{\x}\!\!(\Uparrow_{\Sigma}\!(s))$. Now we can use Lemma~\ref{lemma1.2} repeatedly.
nodes.statement_short: Iterate the one-variable lemma along $\Delta$, using $\Uparrow_{\Sigma,\x}\!(s)\equiv\Uparrow_{\x}\!(\Uparrow_{\Sigma}\!(s))$.

nodes.name: Subject reduction, part two
nodes.statement: $ $\\ Suppose\\ $\Gamma,\x,\Delta\vdash M$ is derivable and\\ $\Gamma,\x,\Delta\vdash M\ri_{\alpha_2} \Gamma,\y,\Delta\vdash\, \Uparrow_{\Delta}\!\langle\pi_{\y}\mi \y\is \x\rangle\ci M$;\\ then\\ $\Gamma,\y,\Delta\vdash\, \Uparrow_{\Delta}\!\langle\pi_{\y}\mi \y\is \x\rangle\ci M$ is derivable.
nodes.statement_short: The context-renaming rule $\alpha_2$ also preserves derivability.

nodes.name: Proof of Subject reduction, part two
nodes.statement: By Generation lemma $\Gamma,\x,\Delta\vdash M$ is derivable iff $\Gamma\vdash\lambda \x.\lambda\Delta.M$ is derivable. To conclude the proof, it is sufficient to prove the following lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Transport the judgement to $\Gamma\vdash\lambda \x.\lambda\Delta.M$ by the Generation lemma and appeal to the next lemma.

nodes.name: Renaming the outermost binder of $\lambda \x.\lambda\Delta.M$
nodes.statement: Suppose\\ $\Gamma\vdash\lambda \x.\lambda\Delta.M$ is derivable; then\\ $\Gamma\vdash\lambda \y.\lambda\Delta.\Uparrow_{\Delta}\!\langle\pi_{\y}\mi \y\is \x\rangle\ci M$ is derivable.

nodes.name: Proof of the renaming lemma
nodes.statement: We use Theorem~\ref{SubRed1} (the case $\alpha_1$) and Lemma~\ref{lemma31}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the $\alpha_1$ case of Subject reduction, part one with the lifting lemma for $\Uparrow_{\Delta}$.

nodes.name: $\sigma\pi\alpha$
nodes.statement: By $\sigma\pi\alpha$ denote $\lambda\pi$ without $Beta$.

nodes.name: $\pi_{\x_1\ldots\x_n}$
nodes.statement: By $\pi_{\x_1\ldots\x_n}$ denote $(\ldots((\pi_{\x_1}\ci\pi_{\x_2})\ci\ldots)\ci\pi_{\x_n}$

nodes.name: Shape of $\sigma\pi\alpha$-normal substitutions
nodes.statement: Suppose $\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta$ is derivable and $s$ is a $\sigma\pi\alpha$-normal form (with respect to $\arrow$); then $s$ has one of the following forms:\\ $ \begin{array}{lll} (i) & id &\\ (ii) & \pi_{\x_1\ldots\x_n} & (n\geqslant 1)\\ (iii) & \la id\mi N_1\is \y_1\mi\ldots\mi N_k\is \y_k\ra & (k\geqslant 1)\\ (iv) & \la\pi_{\x_1\ldots\x_n}\mi N_1\is \y_1\mi\ldots\mi N_k\is \y_k\ra & (n\geqslant 1, k\geqslant 1) \end{array} $\\
nodes.statement_short: A derivable normal-form substitution is $id$, a chain $\pi_{\x_1\ldots\x_n}$, or a cons over one of these.
assumptions: $\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta$ is derivable and $s$ is a $\sigma\pi\alpha$-normal form (with respect to $\arrow$)
conclusions: then $s$ has one of the following forms:\\ $ \begin{array}{lll} (i) & id &\\ (ii) & \pi_{\x_1\ldots\x_n} & (n\geqslant 1)\\ (iii) & \la id\mi N_1\is \y_1\mi\ldots\mi N_k\is \y_k\ra & (k\geqslant 1)\\ (iv) & \la\pi_{\x_1\ldots\x_n}\mi N_1\is \y_1\mi\ldots\mi N_k\is \y_k\ra & (n\geqslant 1, k\geqslant 1) \end{array} $

nodes.name: Proof of the shape of $\sigma\pi\alpha$-normal substitutions
nodes.statement: The proof is by induction over the structure of $s$ (see Definition~\ref{pervoe}). The set of substitutions of the forms $(i)-(iv)$ contains $id$ and $\pi_{\x}$ for any $\x$. This set is also closed under $\la - \mi N\is \y\ra$ for any $N,\y$. To conclude the proof, it is sufficient to prove the following lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Induction over the structure of $s$: the four shapes are closed under $id$, $\pi_{\x}$ and cons, leaving composition to the next lemma.

nodes.name: Composition of substitutions of the four shapes reduces to one of them
nodes.statement: If $\Gamma\vdash s\ci q\tri\Delta$ is derivable and both $s,q$ belong to $(i),(ii),(iii),(iv)$, then $s\ci q\,$ $\sigma\pi\alpha$-reduces to one of the forms $(i),(ii),(iii),(iv)$.
assumptions: $\Gamma\vdash s\ci q\tri\Delta$ is derivable and both $s,q$ belong to $(i),(ii),(iii),(iv)$
conclusions: then $s\ci q\,$ $\sigma\pi\alpha$-reduces to one of the forms $(i),(ii),(iii),(iv)$.

nodes.name: Proof that composition stays within the four shapes
nodes.statement: Let us considered five cases. \\[5pt] Case 1: $q$ is $id$.\\ $s\ci id\arrow s$\\[5pt] Case 2: $s$ is $id$ and $q$ has the form $\pi_{\z_1\ldots\z_m}$.\\ $id\ci \pi_{\z_1\ldots\z_m}\twoh \pi_{\z_1\ldots\z_m}$\\[5pt] Case 3: $s$ has the form $\pi_{\x_1\ldots\x_n}$ and $q$ has the form $\pi_{\z_1\ldots\z_m}$.\\ $(\pi_{\x_1\ldots\x_n})\ci\pi_{\z_1\ldots\z_m}\twoh \pi_{\x_1\ldots\x_n\z_1\ldots\z_m}$\\[5pt] Case 4: $s$ has the form $\la r\mi N_1\is \y_1\mi\ldots\mi N_k\is \y_k\ra$ and $q$ has the form $\pi_{\z_1\ldots\z_m}$, where $r$ is $id$ or $\pi_{\x_1\ldots\x_n}$. Hence, $s\circ q$ has the form\\ $\la r\mi N_1\is \y_1\mi\ldots\mi N_k\is \y_k\ra\ci\pi_{\z_1\ldots\z_m}$. By Generation lemma, $\y_k= \z_1$,\\ $\y_{k-1}= \z_2$, and so on (see Example~\ref{bedsubst}). \\[5pt] If $k=m$,\,then\\[5pt] $\la r\mi N_1\is \y_1\mi\ldots\mi N_k\is \y_k\ra\ci\pi_{\z_1\ldots\z_m}$\quad is the same as\\ $\la r\mi N_1\is \y_1\mi\ldots\mi N_k\is \y_k\ra\ci\pi_{\y_k\ldots\y_1}\twoh r$\\[5pt] If $k>m$,\,then \\[5pt] $\la r\mi N_1\is \y_1\mi\ldots\mi N_k\is \y_k\ra\ci\pi_{\z_1\ldots\z_m}$\quad is the same as\\ $\la r\mi N_1\is \y_1\mi\ldots\mi N_k\is \y_k\ra\ci\pi_{\y_k\ldots\y_{k-m+1}}\twoh \la r\mi N_1\is \y_1\mi\ldots\mi N_{k-m}\is \y_{k-m}\ra $\\[5pt] If $k<m$,\,then\\[5pt] $\la r\mi N_1\is \y_1\mi\ldots\mi N_k\is \y_k\ra\ci\pi_{\z_1\ldots\z_m}$\quad is the same as\\ $\la r\mi N_1\is \z_k\mi\ldots\mi N_k\is \z_1\ra\ci\pi_{\z_1\ldots\z_m}$\\ If $r$ is $id$, this term reduces to $\pi_{\z_{k+1}\ldots\z_m}$. If $r$ is $\pi_{\x_1\ldots\x_n}$, this term reduces to $\pi_{\x_1\ldots\x_n\z_{k+1}\ldots\z_m}$.\\[5pt] Case 5: $q$ has the form $\la r\mi N_1\is \y_1\mi\ldots\mi N_k\is \y_k\ra$, where $r$ is $id$ or $\pi_{\z_1\ldots\z_m}$.\\ $s\ci\la r\mi N_1\is \y_1\mi\ldots\mi N_k\is \y_k\ra\twoh\la s\ci r\mi s\ci N_1\is \y_1\mi\ldots\mi s\ci N_k\is \y_k\ra$\\ Then we use the previous cases to reduce $s\ci r$.
nodes.statement_short: Five cases on the shapes of $s$ and $q$, the cons-against-$\pi$ case splitting further on $k=m$, $k>m$, $k<m$.

nodes.name: Pure term
nodes.statement: A term $M$ is called \emph{pure} iff it does not contain sub-terms of the shape $s\ci N$.
differentia: it does not contain sub-terms of the shape $s\ci N$

nodes.name: $\sigma\pi\alpha$-normal judgements have pure subjects
nodes.statement: If $\Gamma\vdash M$ is derivable and $\Gamma\vdash M$ is a $\sigma\pi\alpha$-normal form (with respect to $\ri$), then $M$ is pure.
nodes.statement_short: A judgement in $\sigma\pi\alpha$-normal form carries a term free of explicit substitutions.
assumptions: $\Gamma\vdash M$ is derivable and $\Gamma\vdash M$ is a $\sigma\pi\alpha$-normal form (with respect to $\ri$)

nodes.name: Proof that normal judgements have pure subjects
nodes.statement: Suppose $M$ contain a sub-term of the shape $s\ci N$; then $N$ must be a variable (we denote it by $\y$), else we can apply $Abs, App$ or $Clos$. The substitution $s$ is a $\sigma\pi\alpha$-normal form and must have the form $\pi_{\x_1\ldots\x_n}$ (see theorem~\ref{Subnf}), else we can apply $IdVar, ConsVar$ or $New$. Further, $\x_n$ in $(\pi_{\x_1\ldots\x_n})\ci \y$ must coincide with $\y$, else we can apply $\pi_1$ or $\pi_2$. We see that $M$ must be constructed from variables and blocks of the form $(\pi_{\x_1\ldots\x_m\y})\ci \y\quad (m\geqslant 0)$ by using application and abstraction. To conclude the proof, it is sufficient to prove the following lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Rule out every non-pure shape by exhibiting an applicable rule, leaving only blocks $(\pi_{\x_1\ldots\x_m\y})\ci \y$, handled by the next lemma.

nodes.name: Terms built from blocks are pure or admit a renaming
nodes.statement: If $\Gamma\vdash M$ is derivable and $M$ is constructed from variables and blocks of the form $(\pi_{\x_1\ldots\x_m\y})\ci \y\quad(m\geqslant 0)$ by using application and abstraction, then $M$ is pure (this means that $M$ does not contain blocks) or we can apply $\alpha_1$ or $\alpha_2$ to $\Gamma\vdash M$.
assumptions: If $\Gamma\vdash M$ is derivable and $M$ is constructed from variables and blocks of the form $(\pi_{\x_1\ldots\x_m\y})\ci \y\quad(m\geqslant 0)$ by using application and abstraction
conclusions: then $M$ is pure (this means that $M$ does not contain blocks) or we can apply $\alpha_1$ or $\alpha_2$ to $\Gamma\vdash M$.

nodes.name: Proof that block terms are pure or admit a renaming
nodes.statement: The proof is by induction over the structure of $M$. Let us consider four cases.\\[5pt] Case 1: $M$ is a variable. The proof is trivial.\\[5pt] Case 2: $ M$ has the form $(\pi_{\x_1\ldots\x_m\y})\ci \y$. By Generation lemma, $\Gamma\vdash M$ has the form\\ $\Delta\mi\y\mi\x_m\mi\ldots\mi \x_1\vdash (\pi_{\x_1\ldots\x_m\y})\ci \y$ \\ and we can apply $\alpha_2$ , because\\ $FV(\y\mi\x_m\mi\ldots\mi \x_1\vdash (\pi_{\x_1\ldots\x_m\y})\ci \y)=\la\{\y\},\emptyset,\emptyset,\ldots\ra$\\[10pt] Case 3: $M$ has the form $\lambda \x.N$. By Generation lemma, $\Gamma,\x\vdash N$ is derivable. Suppose $N$ contains a block of the form $(\pi_{\x_1\ldots\x_m\y})\ci \y$. By induction hypothesis, we can apply $\alpha_1$ or $\alpha_2$ to $\Gamma,\x\vdash N$. But any application of $\alpha_1$ or $\alpha_2$ to $\Gamma,\x\vdash N$ corresponds to some application of $\alpha_1$ or $\alpha_2$ (and, in some cases, $Abs$) to $\Gamma\vdash\lambda \x.N$. For example,\\ $\Gamma,\x\vdash N\ri_{\alpha_2}\Gamma,\y \vdash\la\pi_{\y}\mi \y\is \x\ra\ci N$\\ corresponds to\\ $\Gamma\vdash\lambda \x.N\ri_{\alpha_1}\Gamma\vdash\lambda \y.\la\pi_{\y}\mi \y\is \x\ra\ci N$\\[10pt] Case 4: $M$ has the form $NL$. By Generation lemma, $\Gamma\vdash N$ and $\Gamma\vdash L$ are derivable. Suppose one of these terms contains a block of the form $(\pi_{\x_1\ldots\x_m\y})\ci \y$. For clarity, let it be $N$. By induction hypothesis, we can apply $\alpha_1$ or $\alpha_2$ to $\Gamma\vdash N$. I claim that we can apply $\alpha_1$ or $\alpha_2$ to $\Gamma\vdash NL$. For the case $\alpha_1$ is nothing to prove, because any $\alpha_1$-redex in $N$ occurs in $NL$ too. For the case $\alpha_2$, suppose that $\Gamma\vdash NL$ has the form $\Sigma,\x,\Delta\vdash NL$. Recall that $FV(NL)=FV(N)\cup FV(L)$, hence $FV(N)\subseteq FV(NL)$. By Lemma~\ref{monotone},\\ $FV(\x,\Delta\vdash N))\subseteq FV(\x,\Delta\vdash NL)$.\\ Hence if $\x\in \bigcup_{i\geqslant 1} FV_i(\x,\Delta\vdash N)$, then $\x\in \bigcup_{i\geqslant 1} FV_i(\x,\Delta\vdash NL)$. If we can apply $\alpha_2$ to $\Sigma,\x,\Delta\vdash N$, then we can apply $\alpha_2$ to $\Sigma,\x,\Delta\vdash NL$.
nodes.statement_short: Induction over the structure of $M$ with four cases: variable, block, abstraction and application.

nodes.name: Name-free terms and name-free substitutions
nodes.statement: The symbols $U,V,W$ range over \emph{name-free terms} and the symbols $u,v,w$ range over \emph{name-free substitutions}. The sets of name-free terms and name-free substitutions are defined inductively as follows: \begin{align*} U,V::&= 1 \mid UV \mid \lambda U \mid u\ci U \\ u,v::&= id \mid \pi \mid \langle u\mi V \rangle \mid u\ci v \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: De Bruijn-style syntax: terms built from $1$, application, abstraction and closure; substitutions from $id$, $\pi$, cons and composition.

nodes.name: The calculus $\lambda\sigma$ in the new notation
nodes.statement: (The calculus $\lambda\sigma$ in the new notation).\\[10pt] $ \begin{array}{ccc} & \ruleone{ U_1\arrow U_2}{ \lambda U_1\arrow\lambda U_2} &\\[20pt] & \ruleone{ U_1\arrow U_2}{ U_1V\arrow U_2V} & \ruleone{ V_1\arrow V_2}{ UV_1\arrow UV_2}\\[20pt] & \ruleone{ u_1\arrow u_2}{u_1\ci U\arrow u_2\ci U} & \ruleone{ U_1\arrow U_2}{u\ci U_1\arrow u\ci U_2}\\[20pt] & \ruleone{ u_1\arrow u_2}{ \langle u_1\mi V \rangle\arrow \langle u_2\mi V\rangle} & \ruleone{ V_1\arrow V_2}{ \langle u\mi V_1 \rangle\arrow \langle u\mi V_2\rangle}\\[20pt] & \ruleone{ u_1\arrow u_2}{ u_1\ci v\arrow u_2\ci v} & \ruleone{ v_1\arrow v_2}{ u\ci v_1\arrow u\ci v_2}\\[20pt] \end{array} $ $ \begin{array}{lll} (Beta) & (\lambda U)V\rightarrow \langle id\mi V\rangle\ci U &\\ (Abs) & u\ci \lambda U\rightarrow\lambda \langle \pi\ci u\mi 1\rangle\ci U &\\ (App) & u\ci UV\rightarrow(u\ci U)(u\ci V) &\\ (ConsVar) & \langle u\mi V\rangle\ci 1\rightarrow V &\\ (IdVar) & id\ci 1\rightarrow 1 &\\ (Clos) & u\ci v\ci V\rightarrow (u\ci v)\ci V &\\ (Ass) & u\ci v\ci w\rightarrow (u\ci v)\ci w &\\ (IdR) & u\ci id\rightarrow u &\\ (IdShift) & id\ci \pi\rightarrow\pi &\\ (ConsShift) & \langle u\mi V\rangle\ci \pi\rightarrow u &\\ (Map) & u\ci \langle v\mi V\rangle\rightarrow\langle u\ci v \mi u\ci V\rangle & \end{array} $\\[5pt]
nodes.statement_short: The classical $\lambda\sigma$ rewriting rules restated with composition written in reverse order.

nodes.name: $\sigma$ and the $\sigma$-normal form $\sigma(U)$
nodes.statement: By $\sigma$ denote $\lambda\sigma$ without $Beta$.\\ By $\sigma(U)$ denote the $\sigma$-normal form of $U$ (this normal form exists and is uniquely defined because $\sigma$ is strongly normalizing and confluent).

nodes.name: The numeral $\underline{n}$
nodes.statement: By definition, put\\ $\underline{n}\equiv\underbrace{((\ldots(\pi\ci\pi)\ci\ldots)\ci\pi)}_{\mbox{\scriptsize $n-1$ times}}\ci 1 \qquad(n\geqslant 1)$

nodes.name: Notation $\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}$ for name-free correspondence
nodes.statement: $(\Gamma\vdash M)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} U$ is shorthand for ``the name-free term $U$ corresponds to the judgement $\Gamma\vdash M$."\\ $(\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} u$ is shorthand for ``the name-free substitution $u$ corresponds to the judgement $\Gamma\vdash s\tri\Delta$."

nodes.name: The rules of correspondence between judgements and name-free terms/substitutions
nodes.statement: (The rules of correspondence between judgements and name-free terms/substitutions).\\[5pt] $ \begin{array}{ll} (i)& (\Gamma,\x\vdash \x)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} 1 \\[5pt] (ii)& \ruleone{(\Gamma\vdash \x)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \underline{n}}{(\Gamma,\y\vdash \x)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \underline{n+1}\using {\quad(\x\neq \y)}}\\[20pt] (iii)& \ruletwo{(\Gamma\vdash M)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} U}{(\Gamma\vdash N)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow } V}{(\Gamma\vdash MN)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} UV}\\[15pt] (iv)& \ruleone{(\Gamma,\x\vdash M)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow } U}{(\Gamma\vdash\lambda \x.M)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \lambda U}\\[15pt] (v)& \ruletwo{(\Gamma\vdash s \tri\Delta)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} u }{(\Delta\vdash M)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow } U}{(\Gamma\vdash s \ci M)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow } u \ci U}\\[15pt] (vi)& (\Gamma\vdash id \tri\Gamma)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} id \\[5pt] (vii)& (\Gamma,\x\vdash\pi_{\x} \tri\Gamma)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \pi \\[5pt] (viii)& \ruletwo{(\Gamma\vdash s \tri\Delta)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} u }{(\Gamma\vdash N)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} V}{(\Gamma\vdash \langle s\mi N\is \x\rangle \tri\Delta ,\x)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \la u\mi V\rangle }\\[15pt] (ix)& \ruletwo{(\Gamma\vdash s \tri\Delta)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} u }{(\Delta\vdash q \tri\Sigma)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} v }{(\Gamma \vdash s \ci q \tri\Sigma)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} u \ci v }\\[20pt] \end{array} $
nodes.statement_short: Nine rules translating a derivable judgement into the corresponding De Bruijn term or substitution.
nodes.definiendum: The rules of correspondence between judgements and name-free terms/substitutions

nodes.name: $(x\vdash x)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} 1$
nodes.statement: $$ (x\vdash x)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} 1 $$

nodes.name: $(x,y \vdash x)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \pi\ci 1$
nodes.statement: $$ \ruleone{(x\vdash x)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} 1}{(x,y \vdash x)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \pi\ci 1} $$

nodes.name: $(x,y \vdash \pi_y\ci x)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \pi\ci 1$
nodes.statement: $$ \ruletwo{(x,y \vdash \pi_y\tri x) \boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \pi}{(x \vdash x) \boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} 1}{(x,y \vdash \pi_y\ci x) \boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} \pi\ci 1} $$

nodes.name: Correspondence value of a variable under $n$ distinct binders
nodes.statement: $(\Gamma,\x,\y_1,\ldots,\y_n\vdash \x)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow}\underline{n+1}$ if $\x\neq \y_1,\ldots,\x\neq \y_n$.

nodes.name: Correspondence implies derivability
nodes.statement: If $(\Gamma\vdash M)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} U$, then $\Gamma\vdash M$ is derivable.

nodes.name: Proof that correspondence implies derivability
nodes.statement: The proof is straightforward, see Definition~\ref{defsequentsder} and Definition~\ref{transfer}.
nodes.statement_short: Asserted as straightforward: the correspondence rules mirror the inference rules one for one.

nodes.name: The relation $\backsimeq$ on judgements
nodes.statement: We write $(\Gamma\vdash M)\backsimeq(\Delta\vdash N)$ iff\\ $(\Gamma\vdash M)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} U$ and\\ $(\Delta\vdash N)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} U$, for some $U$.

nodes.name: $(x,y\vdash x)\backsimeq (x,y\vdash\pi_y\ci x)$
nodes.statement: $(x,y\vdash x)\backsimeq (x,y\vdash\pi_y\ci x)$

nodes.name: Pure name-free term
nodes.statement: A name-free term $U$ is called \emph{pure} if it is constructed from the terms $\underline{n}$ by using application and abstraction.
differentia: it is constructed from the terms $\underline{n}$ by using application and abstraction

nodes.name: Pure terms correspond to pure name-free terms
nodes.statement: If $(\Gamma\vdash M)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} U$ and $ M$ is pure, then $U$ is pure. If $U$ is pure, then $U$ is a $\sigma$-normal form.
assumptions: $(\Gamma\vdash M)\boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} U$ and $ M$ is pure

nodes.name: Proof that pure terms correspond to pure name-free terms
nodes.statement: Each pure term $M$ is constructed from variables by using application and abstraction.
nodes.statement_short: Pure terms contain no closures, so their translations are built only from numerals by application and abstraction.

nodes.name: The lifting operators $\Uparrow(s)$ and $\Uparrow^n\!(s)$
nodes.statement: By definition, put\\ $\Uparrow(s)\equiv\la\pi\ci s\mi 1\ra$ \\ $\Uparrow^n\!(s)\equiv\underbrace{\Uparrow(\ldots(\Uparrow}_{\mbox{\scriptsize $n$ times}}(s))\ldots) $

nodes.name: $\sigma$-invariance of the lifted shift $\la\pi\mi 1\ra$
nodes.statement: For any nameless term $U$,\\ $\sigma(\la\pi\mi 1\ra\ci U)\equiv\sigma(U)$ and\\ $\sigma(\Uparrow^n\!\la\pi\mi 1\ra\ci U)\equiv\sigma(U)$

nodes.name: Proof of $\sigma$-invariance of the lifted shift
nodes.statement: See~\cite{Abadi}, Lemma 3.6.
nodes.statement_short: Deferred to the cited source.

nodes.name: Notation $\overset{T}{\ri\ri}$ and $\overset{T}{\twoh}$ for reduction in a calculus $T$
nodes.statement: By $\overset{T}{\ri\ri}$ and $\overset{T}{\twoh}$ denote (reflexive and transitive) reductions in a calculus $T$ ($T$ may be $\lambda\pi,\sigma\pi\alpha,\lambda\sigma$ or $\sigma$).

nodes.name: $\sigma\pi\alpha$-normal forms project onto $\sigma$-normal forms
nodes.statement: Suppose \\ $\begin{array}{l} \Gamma\vdash M\overset{\sigma\pi\alpha}{\ri\ri}\Sigma\vdash L;\\ \Sigma\vdash L \text{ is a $\sigma\pi\alpha$-normal form (with respect to $\overset{\sigma\pi\alpha}{\ri\ri}$)};\\ (\Gamma\vdash M) \boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} U;\\ (\Sigma\vdash L) \boldsymbol{\Rightarrow} V; \end{array}$\\[5pt] then $V$ is a $\sigma$-normal form and $U\overset{\sigma}{\twoh}V$.
nodes.statement_short: Translating a $\sigma\pi\alpha$-normalising reduction gives a $\sigma$-reduction to a $\sigma$-normal form.
assumptions: \Sigma\vdash L \text{ is a $\sigma\pi\alpha$-normal form (with respect to $\overset{\sigma\pi\alpha}{\ri\ri}$)};
